title: Keep S3 encryption args consistent across single-shot and multipart upload paths
answers: add a new S3 upload option that must apply to large files too
which S3 upload args are forwarded to multipart uploads
why small artifacts encrypt but large artifacts do not
body:
Invariant: any server-side encryption argument honored by the single-request upload path must also reach the multipart path, because files above the threshold take _multipart_upload while smaller files take _upload_file.
Enforced by: the allow-list inside OptimizedS3ArtifactRepository._get_multipart_upload_encryption_args, which is the only place that decides what create_multipart_upload receives.
What breaks if skipped: uploads succeed for small files but fail with access denied for files above the multipart threshold on SSE-enforcing buckets.
When adding a key, add it to that allow-list and add a parametrized case in the multipart encryption test. Do not add SSE-C keys without also propagating them to upload_part and complete_multipart_upload.
applies: Any change to which S3 upload extra args are sent by OptimizedS3ArtifactRepository.
says: Uploading large model artifacts fails with access denied on encrypted cloud storage buckets.
Small artifact uploads succeed but large files fail when saving to cloud storage.
Multi-gigabyte model artifacts fail to upload while small configuration files upload normally.
Large file uploads get rejected by cloud storage buckets requiring server side encryption.
Ensure custom encryption settings apply to large file uploads as well as small files.
search: Server-side encryption arguments supported by single-request uploads must also reach multipart uploads in OptimizedS3ArtifactRepository. Files exceeding the size threshold switch from _upload_file to _multipart_upload, and omissions in the allow-list within _get_multipart_upload_encryption_args cause access-denied errors on SSE-enforcing buckets. New encryption keys must be added to that allow-list with parametrized tests in test_multipart_upload_does_not_pass_non_encryption_upload_args, and SSE-C keys must also propagate to upload_part and complete_multipart_upload.
